To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ileostomy output is less than ileal output in normal persons, that the ileostomates do not increase ileal flow after ingestion of medium chain triglycide rich meal, that the ileal flow is increased after long chain triglycerides rich meal, that ileostomy effluents are of consistently alkaline and high potassium concentration and that sodium and water absorptions are continuously stimulated by a chronic salt depletion in the adapted ileostomy patient.
the ileostomy output is less than ileal content in normal subjects both fasting and after ingestion of a long chain triglycerides rich meal.
fasting ileostomy flow and postprandiol ileal function are different in ileostomate and normal subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
ileostomy function in adapted patients and the effects of the ileal passage on ileal flow in normal subjects.
the adaptation of the ileostomy to the loss of the ileum and colon.
the adaptation of ileostomates to their altered intestinal physiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ileostomy output is a good index of ileal function in the ileostomates.
the ileum in the adapted ileostomy patient has an altered function, which is not necessarily a reflection of the ileum's normal function.
the ileum is not functioning normally after ileostomy formation and adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adapted ileostomy is a useful tool for the study of ileal physiology.
the ileostomates have a reduced ileal flow of sodium and water and that this reduction is independent of the type of meal.
the ileal function is altered in adapted ileostomes and this alteration may contribute to the electrolyte imbalance and dehydration which is a common problem in ileostomate patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in adapted ileostomy, ileal function is different from the normal ileum, and that the ileostomy efflux is not a reliable index of ileal function.
the ileostomates have a different pattern of ileal function compared with normal subjects.
the ileostomy efflux is lower than the ileal flow in normal subjects, and this is not related to the presence or absence of the ileocecal valve.
